name: SafeMoon public burn() after upgrade
summary: Upgrades hours before the incident made burn(address,uint256) callable by anyone, moving any holder's SFM to the bridge burn address. The attacker burned nearly all SFM held by the SFM/WBNB PancakeSwap pair, sync()'d it to an inflated SFM price and sold its own SFM into the WBNB reserve; copycats repeated this on smaller SFM pairs.
notes: burn(address,uint256) became public in implementation 0x8e7877fe (upgrade 0x3307500e); the later upgrade to 0xeb11a0a0, which the exploit ran, is the reset (rule 9). Earlier public burns were all holders burning their own SFM.

SFM taken by burn went to SafeMoon's bridgeBurnAddress 0x678ee231, not to attackers, so it is not counted; loss is the WBNB/BUSD drained from the pairs. Later burn() calls that only moved holders' SFM with no attacker proceeds are griefing, not campaign.

Campaign: every non-self burn() after the anchor through block 26900000 traced for attacker proceeds; only the four 0x586094fc pair drains profited. The exploiter's later 80% return is a recovery and not subtracted.
